An interval is an object `{start, end, label?}` where `start` and `end` are epoch milliseconds (numbers) and `label` is an optional string; `window` is an object `{start, end}` in epoch milliseconds with `start <= end`; `minDurationMs` is a number of milliseconds. Node.js builtins only, no external packages. ESM. Neither function mutates its arguments, and both return fresh plain objects.\n\nOptions: both functions take a final `opts` object, which may be omitted. `opts.now` is optional and defaults to `Date.now`; when present it must be a function or undefined, otherwise a `TypeError` with message `\"now must be a function or undefined\"` is thrown. The results of both functions depend only on their inputs, never on the real clock. `findFreeSlots` additionally supports `opts.offsetMin`, optional, default 0: a number of minutes by which the window is shifted before any comparison — the effective window is `{start: window.start + offsetMin * 60000, end: window.end + offsetMin * 60000}`; when present it must be a finite number, otherwise a `TypeError` with message `\"offsetMin must be a finite number\"` is thrown. Each merged interval is a plain object with `start` (the smallest start in the run), `end` (the largest end in the run) and the label of the run's earliest-starting source interval — with equal starts, the one appearing first in the input — taken verbatim, including when it is undefined, in which case the returned object has no `label` property. No other properties are copied. `mergeIntervals([])` returns `[]`.\n\n`findFreeSlots` merges first (with the same `opts`), clips each merged interval to the effective window (a clipped block that merely touches a window edge, and so has zero length, is dropped), and returns the uncovered sub-ranges of the effective window, ascending, as plain `{start, end}` objects with no `label` property. A returned slot satisfies `end - start >= minDurationMs`, so a gap of exactly `minDurationMs` is included and shorter gaps are never returned; zero-length gaps never appear. With no intersecting intervals the whole effective window is the single candidate slot.\n\n\nNote: work carefully and double-check edge cases before finishing."}],"timestamp":1794116097968}}
